power.title: Power Analysis Check
report:
::: {.callout-tip title="Learn More" collapse="true"}

Power analyses need to contain the following information to be interpretable: the type of power analysis, the statistical test, the software used, sample size, critical alpha criterion, power level, effect size, and an effect size metric. In addition, it is recommended to make sure the power analysis is reproducible (by sharing the code, or a screenshot, of the power analysis), and to provide good arguments for why the study was designed to detect an effect of this size.

For an a-priori power analysis, where the sample size is determined, reporting all information would look like:

> An a priori power analysis for an independent samples t-test, conducted using the pwr.t.test function from pwr (Champely, 2020), indicated that for a Cohen's d = 0.5, an alpha level of 0.05, and a desired power level of 80% required at least 64 participants in each group.

For a sensitivity power analysis, this sentence would look like:

> A sensitivity power analysis for an independent samples t-test, conducted using the pwr.t.test function from pwr (Champely, 2020), indicated that with 64 participants in each group, and an alpha level of 0.05, a desired power level of 80% was reached for an effect size of d = 0.5.

:::

text.text: Background: Elevated blood pressure (BP) in childhood is associated with cardiovascular risk, but its molecular lipid correlates remain poorly characterized.
We investigated the association of plasma lipid species and patterns with concurrent and longitudinal BP phenotypes in school-aged children.
Methods: In the Belgian ENVIRONAGE prospective birth-cohort, 195 children aged 9 to 12 years were examined between July 2021 and September 2024.
A total of 1,232 plasma lipid species were quantified using liquid chromatography-electrospray ionization-tandem mass spectrometry.
Associations with systolic and diastolic BP percentiles were examined using multivariable linear regression with permutationbased family-wise error rate (FWER) correction.
Lipid-set enrichment analysis, with P values from sample permutation to account for correlation among lipid species, evaluated coordinated associations.
Significant findings were examined across longitudinal BP patterns in 177 children with BP measured at ages 4-6 and 9-12.
Findings: Each 1-SD increase in triglyceride (TG) 58:9 fatty acyl (FA) 22:4 was associated with 7.36 higher systolic BP percentile points (95% CI=3.91-10.80; 𝑃 FWER =0.03).
TG 58:9 FA 22:4 was associated with incident (OR=2.78; 95% CI=1.33-5.79) and persistent (OR=2.14; 95% CI=1.22-3.77), but not resolved elevated BP vs stable-normal BP.
Among lipid sets, species with a total carbon number of 38, mainly PC and PE, were inversely enriched with diastolic BP percentile.

Interpretation: Childhood BP was associated with higher levels of a highly polyunsaturated long-chain TG, closely related to current BP elevation and not elevated among children whose BP had normalized.

We searched PubMed for studies published from inception to 13 October 2026, without language restrictions, for human studies, using the following combinations of terms: ("child*" OR "adolescen*") AND ("blood pressure" OR "hypertension") AND ("lipidomic*" OR "lipidome").
Previous pediatric studies have implicated glycerophospholipids, sphingolipids and triglycerides, but most were conducted in specific clinical, dietary, environmental, or ethnic settings.

We found little populationbased evidence from comprehensive lipidome-wide analyses and no studies examining whether lipidomic signatures differ according to longitudinal blood pressure patterns spanning early and later childhood.
In a population-based birth cohort, we measured 1,232 lipid species in plasma from 195 children aged 9-12 years and related them to blood pressure at that age and at ages 4-6 years.
One long-chain, highly unsaturated triglyceride was associated with higher systolic blood pressure.
The triglyceride association was present in children whose blood pressure became or remained elevated, but not in those whose elevated blood pressure had normalized.
Accounting for the correlation among lipids, only one lipid group, phospholipids with 38 carbon atoms, was inversely enriched with diastolic blood pressure.
Together with adult studies linking triglyceride species to hypertension, our findings suggest that a triglyceride species is also associated with blood pressure in children.
The lead triglyceride species was more closely related to current elevation, and was not detectable in children with normal current blood pressure but earlier elevation.

Smaller signatures of earlier blood pressure cannot be excluded, studies with repeated lipidomics and blood pressure assessment from early childhood are needed to determine whether earlier blood pressure leaves a more subtle trace in the lipidome.
Elevated blood pressure (BP) is a major modifiable contributor to cardiovascular disease worldwide [1] and sustained hypertension already affects about 4% of children and adolescents globally [2].

We additionally tested whether signals clustered by lipid class, total carbon number, and degree of unsaturation.

In 177 children with BP measured at both the 4-6-year and 9-12-year childhood follow-up visits, we explored whether BP-associated lipid species and classes differed across stable-normal, incident, persistent, and resolved elevated longitudinal BP patterns.
The study was reported in accordance with Strengthening the Reporting of
The ongoing ENVIRonmental influence ON AGEing in early life (ENVIRONAGE) study is a population-based prospective birth cohort established in 2010 in Limburg, Belgium
The analytical platform initially measured 2,017 lipid species.
Lipid nomenclature was standardized using the rgoslin R package.
Preprocessing was performed in R, version 4.5.0.
Lipid species with missing measurements in more than 35% of participants were excluded.
This filtering removed 785 lipids, leaving 1,232 lipids for analysis.

Among the retained lipids, 8,605 measurements (approximately 3.6% of the lipidomic data matrix) were missing and were imputed using the correlation-based k-nearestneighbour method (kNN-CR), selected on the basis of previous simulation evidence for lipidomic data [24].

Based on BP status at the first (4-6 years) and second (9-12 years) follow-up, children were classified into four categories: stable normal, defined as normal BP at both visits; incident elevated BP, defined as normal BP at 4-6 years and elevated BP or hypertension at 9-12 years; persistent elevated BP, defined as elevated BP or hypertension at both visits; and resolved elevated BP, defined as elevated BP or hypertension at 4-6 years and normal BP at 9-12 years.

For the primary cross-sectional lipidomic analysis of BP at 9-12 years, potential confounders were selected a priori based on hypothesized causal relationships represented in a directed acyclic graph (DAG; Figure S1) and included child age, sex, ethnicity, height, weight, highest parental educational attainment, household smoking, physical activity, screen time, and season of examination.

text.text: Primary analyses comprised crosssectional lipidome-wide association analyses of BP at 9-12 years, followed by LSEA; secondary analyses evaluated whether significant species and enriched lipid classes were also associated with longitudinal BP patterns between 4-6 and 9-12 years.
Cross-sectional lipidome-wide associations with BP at 9-12 years were examined using multivariable linear regression.
Separate models were fitted for each individual lipid species and BP outcome.
Systolic and diastolic BP percentiles were considered the primary outcomes.
Systolic BP, diastolic BP, and MAP, expressed in mmHg, were considered secondary outcomes.

text.text: As exploratory secondary analyses, distributions of these lipid species were visualized across pediatric BP categories and associations with BP category were examined using multinomial logistic regression adjusted for the same covariates of the primary model.
To assess linear trend, BP category was additionally modelled as an ordinal outcome and the P value for the lipid term was used as the test for trend.
Nominal P<0.05 was used for these targeted analyses.

text.text: LSEA was performed using the lipidr package to determine whether coordinated associations with BP occurred within lipid sets defined by lipid class, total carbon number, or degree of unsaturation.
For each primary and secondary BP outcome, lipid 13species were ranked according to the signed t-statistic from the corresponding model.
Positive and negative normalized enrichment scores (NES) indicated lipid sets tending towards positive and inverse associations with BP, respectively.
Lipid sets containing fewer than five measured species were not evaluated.
Enrichment was assessed using the fast gene-set enrichment algorithm implemented through fgsea.

Because lipidr's preranked procedure permutes lipid labels, which assumes independence between species, P values were obtained by permuting BP residuals across children (Freedman-Lane, 50,000 permutations).

Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR)-adjusted P was calculated separately for each BP outcome and set type (lipid class, total carbon number, degree of unsaturation), and FDR-adjusted P<0.05 for was considered evidence of lipid-set enrichment.

text.text: Potential effect modification by sex was examined in exploratory analyses by adding a product term between each standardized lipid concentration and sex to the primary model.
To account for pubertal development, we also tested the interaction model additionally adjusting for the Pubertal Development Scale (PDS) score.

In the subset of 177 children with BP data available at both childhood follow-up visits, we evaluated whether lipid species meeting the lipidome-wide significance threshold and lipid classes showing significant enrichment in the cross-sectional analyses were also associated with longitudinal BP patterns.
Associations of the selected lipid species with BP pattern were assessed using multinomial logistic regression, with stable normal BP as the reference category.

To compare the longitudinal groups directly, the 14multinomial models were repeated with resolved elevated BP as the reference category (incident vs resolved; persistent vs resolved), and persistent elevated BP as the reference for incident vs persistent.
Models were adjusted using the same covariate sets as the cross-sectional models and nominal P<0.05 was considered significant.

text.text: In this population-based study of preadolescent children, TG 58:9 FA 22:4 was positively associated with systolic BP percentile after lipidome-wide multiple-testing correction.

Longitudinal analyses indicated that TG 58:9 FA 22:4 was higher in children with incident or persistent elevated BP than in those whose earlier elevated BP had resolved or those with stable-normal BP, supporting a closer relationship of this specific lipid with current BP elevation.
Although comparable data are lacking in children, adult longitudinal findings show broadly concordant class-level directions.

In the Strong Heart Family Study, higher baseline TG species were associated with 20incident hypertension; longitudinal increases in TG species were positively associated with systolic BP change [16].

text.text: TG 58:9 FA 22:4 is a long-chain (58 carbons in total), highly polyunsaturated (9 double bonds) TG in which MS/MS identified a 22-carbon FA moiety with four double bonds (FA 22:4), compatible with adrenic acid (22:4n-6) [32].

text.text: In our study, it was positively associated primarily with systolic BP, although a similar direction of association was observed across all BP outcomes at nominal P<0.05 and across all model specifications, including additional adjustment for fish and seafood consumption, which argues against habitual fish intake explaining this highly unsaturated TG signal.

text.text: Among Chinese children from minority groups, hypertension was associated with higher longchain, polyunsaturated TGs sharing either the total composition (TG 58:9) or the FA 22:4 residue, whereas a plasmalogen PE containing FA 22:4 was lower [21].

text.text: This suggests that associations of FA 22:4 with BP may depend on the lipid class and metabolic context in which it is incorporated, rather than reflecting a uniform effect.
The magnitude of the association is potentially relevant at population level.

A 1-SD higher TG 58:9 FA 22:4 corresponded to 7.36 systolic BP percentile, ~ 0.31 SD of the systolic BP percentile distribution or ~3 mmHg (based on the ratio of the SDs of systolic BP percentiles and mmHg in our population).
In a pooled analysis of seven cohorts, each 1-unit higher childhood systolic BP z-score was associated with a 34% higher risk of fatal adult cardiovascular events [5].
text.formatted: In a pooled analysis of seven cohorts, each 1-unit higher childhood systolic BP z-score was associated with a 34% higher risk of fatal adult cardiovascular events <ref type="bibr" target="#b4">[5]</ref>.

text.text: The BP difference associated with this lipid is therefore of a magnitude that, if persistent, would be relevant for long-term cardiovascular risk.
Despite no evidence of enrichment for TG as a set, TG 58:9 FA 22:4 lay within a region of predominantly positive associations among longer-chain, more polyunsaturated TG species.

Pediatric evidence was recently reported in a nested case-control lipidomic study of Chinese children, in which several long-chain, highly unsaturated TGs were elevated in children with higher BP [19].

text.text: Potential mechanisms linking TG-rich lipoprotein metabolism to BP include endothelial dysfunction and oxidative stress [33, 34], but this evidence relates to conventional hypertriglyceridemia and cannot be attributed to TG species.

text.text: Adiposity is an important potential determinant of both circulating TG profiles and BP.

In children and adolescents, large, weakly unsaturated TG species were elevated in those suffering from overweight or obesity and decreased with greater reductions in BMI SDS during a lifestyle intervention [17]; while TG-related differences associated with hypertension were substantially attenuated after adjustment for BMI z score [19].
text.formatted: In children and adolescents, large, weakly unsaturated TG species were elevated in those suffering from overweight or obesity and decreased with greater reductions in BMI SDS during a lifestyle intervention <ref type="bibr" target="#b16">[17]</ref>; while TG-related differences associated with hypertension were substantially attenuated after adjustment for BMI z score <ref type="bibr" target="#b18">[19]</ref>.

text.text: In contrast, our lead association (TG 58:9 FA 22:4 with systolic BP percentile) remained relatively stable after weight adjustment and after excluding children with overweight or obesity.

This finding, together with the fact that TG 58:9 FA 22:4 is highly unsaturated, suggests that the observed association may reflect a pathway distinct from adiposity-driven TG accumulation; alternatively, adiposity may still contribute through a pathway that weight adjustment does not capture.

Children with any elevated-BP pattern, including the resolved group, were more often overweight or obese than stable-normal children (26 to 31% vs 11%; Table S1), so adiposity history could contribute to the resolved-group signals.

text.text: Phospholipid species with 38 total carbons, mostly PC and PE carrying 20-and 22carbon chains, were inversely associated with diastolic BP, consistent with the borderline PC pattern.
As this set combines several lipid classes and was the only significant set, it should be considered hypothesis-generating.

This study has several strengths, including BP phenotyping via 5 repeated BP standardized measurements; an untargeted, lipid-wide approach across more than 1,200 species in a population-based, not clinically selected or obesity-restricted, pediatric cohort; rigorous correction for multiple testing via a permutation-based empirical family-wise error rate, including lipid-set inference by sample permutation, which accounts for the strong correlation among lipid species that is ignored by the commonly used preranked procedure [35]; extensive sensitivity analyses addressing confounding by adiposity, pubertal timing, seasonality, and comorbidity; and longitudinal BP phenotyping spanning early and later childhood.

text.text: This study also has limitations.
The estimate for the lead lipid (β=7.36) is below the MDE (8.68), so smaller true effects may have gone undetected and the estimate may be inflated, as is common in discovery analyses.
This is a single-cohort study without external validation.
BP patterns rest on one oscillometric visit at each age, so some children may be misclassified and regression to the mean may contribute to the resolved group.
Lipids were measured once, in preadolescence, and circulating lipid profiles are dynamic [36], so we cannot tell when the differences arose.
text.formatted: Lipids were measured once, in preadolescence, and circulating lipid profiles are dynamic <ref type="bibr" target="#b35">[36]</ref>, so we cannot tell when the differences arose.

text.text: The cohort is predominantly of European ancestry, limiting generalizability to other populations.

Blood sampling was not standardized with respect to fasting status, which may contribute to interindividual variation in lipid species; adjustment for time of blood 23collection may only partially account for this source of variability.

We acknowledge that our sex-interaction findings are exploratory and require replication, although plausibility is supported by lipidomic sexual dimorphism in preadolescents [37] and previous evidence that metabolic correlates of BP differ between males and females during adolescence [22].
text.formatted: We acknowledge that our sex-interaction findings are exploratory and require replication, although plausibility is supported by lipidomic sexual dimorphism in preadolescents <ref type="bibr" target="#b36">[37]</ref> and previous evidence that metabolic correlates of BP differ between males and females during adolescence <ref type="bibr" target="#b21">[22]</ref>.

text.text: From a translational perspective, our findings suggest that normalization of BP may coincide with normalization of BP-lipid-associated signatures.

Previous life-course studies indicate that cardiovascular target-organ risk is substantially attenuated when elevated childhood BP resolves, although a small residual risk cannot be excluded [7, 38, 39].
text.formatted: Previous life-course studies indicate that cardiovascular target-organ risk is substantially attenuated when elevated childhood BP resolves, although a small residual risk cannot be excluded <ref type="bibr" target="#b6">[7,</ref> <ref type="bibr" target="#b37">38,</ref> <ref type="bibr" target="#b38">39]</ref>.

text.text: However, longitudinal studies with repeated lipidomics and cardiovascular phenotyping are needed to determine whether persistent signatures exist among children whose earlier elevated BP has resolved.
In conclusion, our study found TG 58:9 FA 22:4 associated with systolic BP in preadolescents and was closely associated with current BP elevation.
Replication in independent cohorts with repeated lipidomics is needed.

text.text: Mother-newborn pairs are recruited at birth at East-Limburg Hospital in Genk, Belgium, and are subsequently invited to participate in two follow-up examinations later in life (between 4 and 6 years of age and between 9 and 12 years of age).
At enrolment, eligibility required mothers to be able to complete questionnaires in Dutch and to have not planned a caesarean section.

The ENVIRONAGE study was conducted in accordance with the principles of the Declaration of Helsinki and was approved by the ethics committees of Hasselt University and East-Limburg Hospital (Genk, Belgium; reference nos.
Written informed consent was obtained from the mothers at cohort enrolment.

For the childhood follow-ups, written informed consent was obtained from the parents or legal guardians, and assent was obtained from the participating children.The present study includes 195 children participating between July 2021 and September 2024 in the second childhood follow-up examination at 9-12 years of age, who provided a blood sample for lipidomic profiling and had a valid BP measurement. 177 of these children also had a valid BP measurement at the first follow-up examination at 4-6 years of age.
The number of participants included in individual statistical models depended on covariate availability, as specified in the Results.
Lipidomics During the follow-up examination at 9-12 years of age, venous blood was collected by a trained fieldworker.
Plasma was separated and stored at -80°C until lipidomic analysis.

Lipidomic analyses were performed at the Lipometrix lab at KU Leuven (Leuven, Belgium) using liquid chromatography electrospray ionization tandem mass spectrometry (LC-ESI-MS/MS) on a Nexera X2 UHPLC system (Shimadzu) coupled with hybrid triple quadrupole/linear ion trap mass spectrometer (6500+ QTRAP system; AB SCIEX).

Lipids were quantified by scheduled multiple-reaction monitoring using internal standard signals and adhered to the guidelines of the Lipidomics Standards Initiative (LSI) (level 2 type quantification as defined by the LSI).
Detailed extraction procedures, chromatographic conditions, mass-spectrometry settings, and lipid-class-specific transitions are provided in the Supplemental Methods.

Sensitivity analyses of lipid species meeting the lipidome-wide significance threshold and lipid classes showing significant enrichment in the cross-sectional analyses were conducted by repeating the analyses by: (i) additionally adjusting for the PDS score; (ii) removing child weight from the adjustment; (iii) replacing, in the adjustment set, season of examination with average daily temperature on the day of examination among children with available meteorological information; (iv) additionally adjusting for fish and seafood consumption; (v) excluding children with reported cardiometabolic conditions (n=2); (vi) excluding children with reported corticosteroid use (n=5); and (vii) excluding children with overweight or obesity (n=35).

In addition, the complete lipidome-wide and lipid-set enrichment analyses, including the longitudinal analyses, were repeated using a basic model including a reduced covariate set (child sex, age, height, ethnicity, season, time of blood collection and plasma storage duration), which does not require complete data on weight, parental education, household smoking, physical activity and screen time and therefore retains a larger sample (N = 195 cross-15-
